'''Henry A. Bent''' (December 21, 1926 – January 3, 2015)<ref>{{cite web |title=In memoriam: Professor Henry Albert Bent |url=https://cse.umn.edu/college/feature-stories/memoriam-henry-albert-bent |website=College of Science and Engineering |publisher=University of Minnesota |accessdate=30 March 2020 |date=6 January 2015}}</ref> was a professor of [[physical chemistry]] who studied [[molecular orbital]]s to develop [[Orbital hybridisation|atomic hybridization]] and [[valence bond]] theories.<ref name="CEN obit">{{cite journal |last1=Ainsworth |first1=Susan J. |title=Henry A. Bent |journal=Chemical and Engineering News |date=23 March 2015 |volume=93 |issue=12 |page=44 |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/93/i12/HenryBent.html |accessdate=29 March 2020}}</ref> [[Bent's rule]], which predicts the orbital hybridization of a central atom as a function of the [[electronegativity|electronegativities]] of the [[substituent]]s attached to it, is named for him. 

In [[thermodynamics]] he developed a global approach now known as "entropy analysis" for the [[entropy]] component of [[thermodynamic free energy]] in relation to the [[second law of thermodynamics]] and the [[Spontaneous process|spontaneity]] of various chemical processes.<ref>{{cite journal |title= Teaching Entropy Analysis in the First-Year High School Course and Beyond |first= Thomas H. |last= Bindel |journal= J. Chem. Educ. |year= 2004 |volume= 81 |issue= 11 |pages= 1585–1594 |doi= 10.1021/ed081p1585 }}</ref> 

Bent was also interested in the [[periodic law]]s of the elements and promoted the [[Alternative periodic tables#Left-step periodic table (Janet, 1928)|left-step periodic table]] based on orbital-filling rules.<ref>{{cite journal |title= New Ideas in Chemistry from Fresh Energy for the Periodic Law (Henry A. Bent) |first= A. Truman |last= Schwartz |journal= J. Chem. Educ. |year= 2007 |volume= 84 |issue= 9 |pages= 1431–1432 |doi= 10.1021/ed084p1431 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
